import os
import tempfile
import pytest
from doorstop.core.document import Document
from doorstop.core.tree import Tree
from doorstop.core.item import Item
from doorstop.core.vcs import mockvcs  # use mock VCS for isolation


@pytest.fixture
def temp_dir():
    """Create a temporary directory for test documents."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        yield d


def test_U01_2__Use_Cases_Us__TC_001(temp_dir):
    """
    User logs into Doorstop and views requirements as a document.
    Expected: Doorstop displays the requirements in a document format,
    and the user can interact with the document to view details.
    """
    # Create a new document in the temp directory
    doc_path = os.path.join(temp_dir, "doc1")
    os.makedirs(doc_path, exist_ok=True)
    doc = Document.new(doc_path)

    # Add a couple of items to the document
    item1 = doc.add_item(level=1)
    item1.text = "Requirement 1"
    item2 = doc.add_item(level=2)
    item2.text = "Requirement 1.1"

    # Build the tree for the document
    tree = Tree(doc)
    # The tree should contain the document and its items
    assert len(tree) >= 1, "Tree should contain at least the root document"
    # Verify that the items are present in the tree
    found_uids = {itm.uid for itm in tree.document.items}
    assert item1.uid in found_uids
    assert item2.uid in found_uids

    # Simulate user interaction: retrieve item details
    # The Document API provides a method to get an item by UID
    retrieved = tree.document.get_item(item1.uid)
    assert retrieved is not None, "Item should be retrievable by UID"
    assert retrieved.text == "Requirement 1", "Item text should match"

    # Ensure that the document can be rendered (e.g., via Tree.draw)
    # The draw method returns a string representation of the tree
    rendered = tree.draw()
    assert isinstance(rendered, str), "Rendered output should be a string"
    assert "Requirement 1" in rendered, "Rendered output should contain item text"


def test_U01_2__Use_Cases_Us__TC_002(temp_dir):
    """
    User views requirements without adding any.
    Expected: Doorstop displays a message indicating that no requirements have been added yet,
    and the user is prompted to add requirements.
    """
    # Create a new document with no items
    doc_path = os.path.join(temp_dir, "doc_empty")
    os.makedirs(doc_path, exist_ok=True)
    doc = Document.new(doc_path)

    # Build the tree
    tree = Tree(doc)

    # The tree should have length 1 (only the document)
    assert len(tree) == 1, "Tree should contain only the root document"

    # The document should report no items
    assert len(doc.items) == 0, "Document should have no items"

    # Simulate rendering: Tree.draw should indicate empty state
    rendered = tree.draw()
    assert isinstance(rendered, str), "Rendered output should be a string"
    # The default draw implementation may not include a specific message,
    # but we can check that it does not contain any item text
    assert "Requirement" not in rendered, "Rendered output should not contain any requirement text"

    # Since the UI layer is not available in this test, we consider the absence of items
    # as the condition that would trigger the "no requirements" message in the GUI.


def test_U01_2__Use_Cases_Us__TC_003(temp_dir, monkeypatch):
    """
    User views requirements during a technical error.
    Expected: Doorstop encounters a technical error and displays an error message,
    and the user is notified of the error and advised to try again later.
    """
    # Create a new document with an item
    doc_path = os.path.join(temp_dir, "doc_error")
    os.makedirs(doc_path, exist_ok=True)
    doc = Document.new(doc_path)
    doc.add_item(level=1)

    # Build the tree
    tree = Tree(doc)

    # Monkeypatch the Tree.draw method to raise an exception simulating a technical error
    def faulty_draw(*args, **kwargs):
        raise RuntimeError("Simulated rendering failure")

    monkeypatch.setattr(tree, "draw", faulty_draw)

    # Attempt to render and capture the exception
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="Simulated rendering failure"):
        tree.draw()

    # In a real GUI, this exception would be caught and an error message displayed.
    # Here we assert that the exception propagates as expected, indicating a technical error.
